candidates.title: 2ManyDJs, Rory Phillips
candidates.summary: The Dewaele brothers (Soulwax) bring their 2ManyDJs mashup set to Good Room, with Rory Phillips opening. Thursday night, 10pm to 4am, 21+, tickets $30 to $40 on RA. Good Room holds a few hundred people and the Good Room floor has a proper sound system.
candidates.fit: This is the Thursday slot he actually uses, in a small Greenpoint room rather than a warehouse, and 2ManyDJs will run Daft Punk-adjacent edits into disco and house all night. No bottle service, no line culture, you can stand ten feet from the booth.

candidates.title: Elsewhere Halloween: Major League DJz, SAIDAH, D Stone, Ariel Lights b2b Sissy Elliott
candidates.summary: Elsewhere turns the whole building over for Halloween with South Africa's Major League DJz headlining The Hall, SAIDAH and D Stone in Zone One, and Ariel Lights b2b Sissy Elliott in the Loft. Doors 10:30pm, music to 4am. Tickets from roughly $47 on Dice.
candidates.fit: Amapiano is exactly the phase he's in, and Major League DJz are the people who exported it. Costume night, multiple rooms, Bushwick, and none of it is the Manhattan Afrobeats-with-table-minimum version.

candidates.title: CircoLoco Halloween: Dixon, ANOTR, Jimi Jules, Aline Umber, Jamback, Krol, Rossi
candidates.address: Building 293, Brooklyn Navy Yard, 63 Flushing Ave, Brooklyn, NY
candidates.price_text: face value not confirmed; resale listings around $240
candidates.summary: CircoLoco takes over the Brooklyn Storehouse warehouse in the Navy Yard for Halloween weekend, with Saturday headlined by Dixon alongside ANOTR and Jimi Jules. 10pm start, 21+. Primary tickets were close to gone when checked; most of what is left is resale.
candidates.fit: Dixon is Innervisions, which is the deep end of the melodic house he already loves, and the Navy Yard warehouse is a ten-minute car ride from Fort Greene. This is his once-in-a-while big night, closer to the Kx5 register than a club booking.

candidates.title: CircoLoco Halloween Sunday: Prospa, Jimi Jules, Chloé Caillet
candidates.address: Building 293, Brooklyn Navy Yard, 63 Flushing Ave, Brooklyn, NY
candidates.price_text: face value not confirmed; resale listings around $197
candidates.summary: The Sunday closer of CircoLoco's Halloween run at Brooklyn Storehouse runs noon to 11pm with Prospa, Jimi Jules and Chloé Caillet. Daytime warehouse party in the Navy Yard, 21+. Listings showed very few tickets left when checked.
candidates.fit: A warehouse day party that ends before midnight is the version of this he can actually do as a dad, and it is the same format as the BQE day party he loved. Home in Fort Greene in fifteen minutes.

candidates.title: Halloween Nonstop: DJ Stingray 313, Convextion, Juliana Huxtable, Rene Wise + more
candidates.time_text: Friday 10pm straight through to Sunday night; Sunday daytime sets from early morning
candidates.summary: Nowadays runs its weekend-long Nonstop in full Halloween mode, with DJ Stingray 313, Convextion, Juliana Huxtable, Rene Wise, Imogen, Cotton, Tammy Lakkis and more across Friday night into Sunday. Tickets by session on RA; the backyard and indoor floor both run.
candidates.fit: The Sunday daytime block is the move for him — serious techno and electro, outdoors, home before dinner, instead of a 4am peak. Nowadays is the no-phones, no-bro-energy room he wants more of.

candidates.title: Xanadu x Choke Hole x Function: WITCHSLAP (skate, drag wrestling, dance party)
candidates.time_text: evening into late night; exact door time not confirmed
candidates.summary: A Halloween-weekend mashup of roller skating, Choke Hole drag wrestling, live performance and a dance party, listed on RA for Friday October 30 at Xanadu in Brooklyn. Door time and price were not posted on the listing page.
candidates.fit: This is All Night Skate plus drag wrestling plus a costume party in one building, which is three things off his list at once. Check the door time before you commit, the listing was thin on details.

candidates.title: Tiki Disco Halloween
candidates.price_text: not listed; Good Room nights typically $20 to $35
candidates.summary: Tiki Disco, the long-running Brooklyn disco and house party, takes Good Room for Halloween night. Costumes expected, tickets via RA.
candidates.fit: If the warehouse options feel like too much, this is the costume dance night in a small room version: disco and house records, people in actual costumes, and a bar you can get to. Same energy as the ABBA night he went to, better music policy.

candidates.title: Papi Juice Halloween
candidates.price_text: not confirmed on the calendar listing
candidates.summary: Papi Juice, the Brooklyn art collective and party now in its second decade, takes over all of Elsewhere for a Halloween edition on Friday October 30, doors 10:30pm. Tickets through Eventbrite via the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Full-venue, costume-mandatory, community-run party with a Latin and Afro-diasporic music policy, which is where his reggaeton and Afrobeats tastes overlap. It is a scene party, not a promoter product.

candidates.title: John Summit: CTRL Escape Arena Tour (with Cassian)
candidates.price_text: resale listings seen from about $243; primary pricing varies by tier
candidates.summary: John Summit plays two nights at Barclays Center on Saturday November 28 and Sunday November 29, 7pm, with Cassian and Jackie Hollander on the bill. Tickets through Ticketmaster and Live Nation.
candidates.fit: Tier 1 artist, Thanksgiving weekend, and the arena is a walk from his apartment. This is the two-or-three-times-a-year big room show, and Cassian opening means the first hour is actually melodic rather than filler.

candidates.title: 22 Years of FIXED: Kelly Lee Owens (DJ set), JDH & Dave P
candidates.summary: FIXED, the 22-year-old New York party run by JDH and Dave P, celebrates its anniversary at Good Room with a DJ set from Kelly Lee Owens. Ivan Berko plays all night in the Bad Room.
candidates.fit: A party that has been running since before most Brooklyn clubs existed, in a 300-ish capacity room, with a headliner who plays melodic techno with actual songs in it. Exactly the 'you had to know someone' register he asks for.

candidates.title: Cut Copy (DJ set), Disco Bambino, Kristine Barilli + more
candidates.price_text: not confirmed on the calendar listing
candidates.summary: Cut Copy plays a DJ set across the full venue at Elsewhere on Friday November 13, doors 10:30pm, with ራሄል (Rachel), Disco Bambino, Kristine Barilli and Gravitational across the other rooms.
candidates.fit: Cut Copy DJing is indie-disco and Italo rather than the live show, which lands between his Daft Punk touchstone and his Empire of the Sun streak. Full-venue Elsewhere means you can bail upstairs when a room isn't working.

candidates.title: NY Night Train: 21st Annual Haunted Hop
candidates.summary: Jonathan Toubin's long-running soul-45s costume dance party returns to Knockdown Center for its 21st Halloween edition, listed by the venue for Friday, October 30. Expect a costume contest, live bands and all-vinyl rock and soul rather than club DJs.
candidates.fit: A 21-year-old annual costume dance party run by one guy and his record crates — the word-of-mouth tradition, not the listicle Halloween party. Good Friday with friends who want to dress up and actually dance.

candidates.title: Brutalismus 3000 presents B3K Invites NY (with SPFDJ, Dorian Electra DJ set, eera, Nurse)
candidates.price_text: resale listings from about $64; face value not confirmed
candidates.summary: Berlin duo Brutalismus 3000 headline their own curated night at Knockdown Center on Friday November 6, with SPFDJ, eera, Dorian Electra (DJ set) and Nurse. Listed across Bandsintown, AXS and Songkick; the Knockdown event page URL was not reachable when checked.
candidates.fit: Berlin act, Berlin label friends, in the best warehouse room in the city. Loud, fast and extremely not a Time Out pick, and it scratches the same itch as the German music in his library.

candidates.title: LCD Soundsystem (three nights)
candidates.summary: LCD Soundsystem play a three-night run at Knockdown Center on November 19, 20 and 21 at 8pm, per the AXS venue calendar and Bandsintown. Capacity at Knockdown is a fraction of an arena, so these will move.
candidates.fit: A band that plays dance music in a warehouse instead of an arena, which is the trade he keeps saying he wants. If any of the three nights still has tickets, it is a book-now.

candidates.title: 240 Months of Riotvan: Panthera Krause, Peter Invasion, Timo Lee
candidates.summary: The Riotvan label marks 20 years at Good Room with Leipzig's Panthera Krause plus Peter Invasion and Timo Lee, with Mike Simonetti playing all night in the Bad Room.
candidates.fit: German label, German headliner, small Greenpoint room, and a Bad Room with Mike Simonetti playing records all night if the main floor gets busy. Low-key version of the Berlin lane.

candidates.title: 718 Sessions 24th Anniversary with Danny Krivit
candidates.time_text: Sunday session; start time not yet posted
candidates.summary: Danny Krivit's 718 Sessions celebrates 24 years at Good Room on Sunday November 15, with Go Kiryu and Hirame in the Bad Room. Good Room's calendar lists the date but no ticket link or door time yet.
candidates.fit: Krivit is a genuine New York institution who has been edit-ing disco records since the seventies, and 718 Sessions is a dancing crowd, not a watching crowd. A Sunday party he can leave at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Juan MacLean (all night long)
candidates.summary: The Juan MacLean plays an all-night set at Good Room on Saturday November 21, with Tavish and Gee Dee in the Bad Room. Tickets via RA.
candidates.fit: One DJ, one room, six hours, which means the set actually goes somewhere instead of resetting every 90 minutes. DFA-school house in a small room is squarely his taste.

candidates.title: FIXED with HAAi, JDH & Dave P
candidates.summary: HAAi headlines FIXED at Good Room on Saturday December 5, with residents JDH and Dave P, plus JEWELSSEA and QRTR playing all night in the Bad Room. Tickets via RA.
candidates.fit: HAAi plays melodic, psychedelic techno with proper builds, which is the Tinlicker and Rebūke end of his library played by someone who takes risks. Small room, December, easy to get a group of three in.

candidates.title: Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit
candidates.time_text: early prelims from the afternoon, main card 9pm ET
candidates.summary: The UFC's annual Madison Square Garden card. Ciryl Gane vs Josh Hokit for the heavyweight title headlines, with Kayla Harrison vs Amanda Nunes for the women's bantamweight belt as the co-main and Caio Borralho vs Yousri Belgaroui also on the main card. Main card starts 9pm ET; tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster via the UFC event page, and UFC also sells VIP packages separately.
candidates.fit: This is the one big-spectacle fight night of the fall in New York, and a two-title-fight card at the Garden is exactly the few-times-a-year splurge he says is worth it. He trains Muay Thai and teaches Krav Maga; a Harrison-Nunes rematch is the kind of card his gym crew will actually talk about afterward.

candidates.title: WWE: Raw & SmackDown - Two Shows, One Night
candidates.time_text: evening, doors typically about an hour before bell
candidates.summary: Barclays Center is running both WWE Raw and SmackDown back to back on a single night, listed on the arena's own events calendar for November 2. Tickets are sold through the Barclays Center event page. Exact bell times and the card were not posted on the calendar listing.
candidates.fit: He already likes live pro wrestling as bar programming; this is the full-volume arena version, and it is a fifteen-minute walk from Fort Greene. It is a Monday, which he normally skips, but a double taping in his own backyard is the kind of exception worth making.

candidates.title: New York Knicks vs Brooklyn Nets
candidates.summary: The city game: Knicks host the Nets at Madison Square Garden on Monday, November 2 at 7:30pm per the official Knicks schedule. Secondary-market listings were quoted around the high $190s when checked, which is not a primary-source price.
candidates.fit: A Knicks-Nets night is the one regular-season game with a group-chat argument built into it, and half his crew lives on the Brooklyn side. Monday is normally a no, so only take this if the Pacers and Heat dates do not work.

candidates.title: Knicks NBA Cup night at the Garden
candidates.summary: The official Knicks home schedule lists December 10 at 8pm as 'Potential NBA Cup/Regular Season: New York Knicks v TBD' at Madison Square Garden. If the Knicks advance, this becomes a knockout game with a trophy attached; if not, it reverts to a regular-season date. Opponent and final status are not yet set.
candidates.fit: It is a Thursday, his main weeknight slot, and a Cup knockout game is the closest thing to a playoff atmosphere you can buy in December. Worth holding tickets now given the opponent is still TBD and prices move once the bracket is set.

candidates.title: New York Knicks vs Miami Heat
candidates.summary: Knicks host Miami at the Garden on Friday, November 27, the night after Thanksgiving, per the published 2026-27 Knicks home schedule. Heat-Knicks remains one of the genuinely nasty matchups in the East. Tip time and pricing were not confirmed on a primary arena page.
candidates.fit: Black Friday with the guys instead of a mall: an old-school grudge matchup on a Friday night, which is one of his two weekend evening slots. Easy sell to a group that spent last spring in bars watching the Knicks.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Nets vs Detroit Pistons
candidates.summary: Nets host Detroit on Friday, October 30 at Barclays Center, listed on the arena's own events calendar with tickets through Ticketmaster. Detroit has become a watchable young team, and Barclays lower bowl is usually gettable on short notice. Prices were not verified.
candidates.fit: It is the only live pro sport in walking distance of Fort Greene this week. Not the Knicks, and he knows it, but it is a Friday night, you can decide at 5pm, and you are home by eleven.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Nets vs Orlando Magic
candidates.summary: Nets host the Magic on Friday, November 20 at Barclays Center per the arena calendar. Orlando brings one of the more physical young rosters in the East. Tip time and pricing were not confirmed beyond the calendar listing.
candidates.fit: Backup Friday option in his front yard when the Garden dates are too much money or too much travel. Walk over, eat on Vanderbilt after, done.

candidates.title: UFC 335: Oliveira vs Lopes
candidates.summary: UFC's December numbered card, Charles Oliveira vs Diego Lopes, is set for Saturday, December 12 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, with the main card at 9pm ET and streaming on Paramount+ per the official UFC events page. Not a New York event, but it is the biggest fight night of the radar window you can watch here.
candidates.fit: The one to build a living-room or back-room night around in December if he is not flying anywhere. Oliveira is the kind of fighter his Kings Combat crew will actually show up for.

candidates.title: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs Stirling
candidates.summary: UFC's Doha card featuring Jiri Prochazka vs Bo Nickal-era light heavyweight contender Carlos Stirling runs Saturday, November 21 with the main card at 1pm ET, per the official UFC schedule. Because of the time zone, the whole card plays out over a New York Saturday afternoon on Paramount+.
candidates.fit: A fight card that starts at 1pm is the rare one a dad can actually watch all the way through. Prochazka is the most entertaining striker in the division, which matters to someone who trains striking.

candidates.title: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs Nolan
candidates.summary: A lightweight-headlined Fight Night from the UFC APEX on Halloween night, prelims at 5pm ET and main card at 8pm ET, streaming on Paramount+ per the UFC's official events page. It is a small-room APEX card, not an arena show.
candidates.fit: Only worth noting because it falls on Halloween Saturday: if the costume plans collapse, the fights are on from 5pm. Thin card, so treat it as background, not the plan.

candidates.title: Stout Season 2026 (5th Annual)
candidates.price_text: ticketed on Eventbrite; price not listed on the brewery's own page
candidates.summary: Other Half's fifth annual stout festival at the original Centre Street taproom, indoor/outdoor, 12pm to 4pm on Saturday December 5. The ticket covers unlimited draft pours from 40-plus visiting breweries (Anchorage, Side Project, Trillium, Toppling Goliath, Firestone Walker, Drekker, Hop Butcher and more), access to the Snowbird Lounge, surprise magnum pours, with food and Snowbirds bottle releases for sale. 21+, no pets, tickets are limited.
candidates.fit: This is the beer-nerd version of his sunny-day-at-Strong-Rope habit: a walkable-from-Fort-Greene brewery yard, three hours, done by late afternoon, built for two or three guys with a tasting list and opinions. Buy now, these sell out.

candidates.title: RAW WINE New York 2026
candidates.summary: The tenth New York edition of RAW WINE, the organic, biodynamic and low-intervention wine fair, lands at Industry City on Sunday November 8 and Monday November 9, 2026. Hundreds of growers pour their own wine and you talk to the person who made it; Sunday runs noon to 6pm, Monday noon to 5pm (Monday skews trade).
candidates.fit: He asked for natural wine fairs specifically, and Sunday daytime is his slot. It is the opposite of a listicle bar: you spend three hours talking to winemakers, not waiting in a line. Works as a date-day with the wife or as a two-guys afternoon.

candidates.title: Maccabee Bar (Hanukkah pop-up cocktail bar)
candidates.summary: Naomi Levy's Hanukkah-themed pop-up cocktail bar, which in past New York years has taken over Ollie in the West Village with latkes, sufganiyot and holiday cocktails. Hanukkah 2026 begins the evening of December 4, so a December run is the expectation. I could not confirm 2026 dates, venue or reservations before my research budget ran out.
candidates.fit: He has already been to the Hanukkah cocktail bar and loved it, and it is the one December drink booking that needs to be grabbed the day it opens. Treat this as a reservation alert, not a confirmed pick.

candidates.title: Choke Hole (drag wrestling) at Pioneer Works
candidates.summary: Choke Hole is the New Orleans-born queer drag-wrestling league that has been staging full spectacles in Brooklyn since 2018, most recently a two-night run at Pioneer Works in Red Hook (the 2025 ARMAGEDDON nights were November 11 and 12). No 2026 New York date is posted on the Pioneer Works program page as of this research.
candidates.fit: Drag wrestling in a Red Hook art space is exactly the bar-programming-gone-weird lane he asked for, and it sits between his Phoenix drag nights and his fight-card habit. Worth a calendar alert: these go on sale quietly and sell out fast.

candidates.title: Loreley Halloween takeover
candidates.summary: Per a NYC Halloween bar guide updated in October 2026, Loreley's Halloween run started October 16 and continues through the holiday, with the final weekend being the busy one. It is a German beer hall with a back garden, so the Halloween build-out comes with liters, not bottle service. Hours and any cover were not confirmed on the venue's own page.
candidates.fit: German beer hall plus Halloween decor is two of his lanes in one room, and it is a walk-in with the guys rather than a ticketed costume party. Thin sourcing: call before you commit the crew.

candidates.title: Whiskey Locker Tasting Dinner featuring Michter's
candidates.summary: Resy lists a Michter's whiskey tasting dinner on Thursday November 5, 2026 at 6:30pm on the Upper West Side, built around the restaurant's whiskey locker program. Format, pour list and price per person were not shown and could not be confirmed.
candidates.fit: Thursday is his night and a seated whiskey dinner with a distillery rep is the kind of drink event he asked for, but the room is not his scene. Only worth the subway if the pour list is serious; confirm first.

candidates.title: SSAW Brooklyn 2nd Anniversary Tasting Menu
candidates.summary: Resy's New York events page lists a one-night second-anniversary special tasting menu at SSAW in Brooklyn on Saturday November 7, 2026. Seating times and price were not shown in the listing and the restaurant's own page could not be opened to confirm.
candidates.fit: A small Brooklyn kitchen cooking a one-night anniversary menu is the restaurant-in-restaurant register he wants, and Saturday night with the wife is the obvious use. Verify the price and the seating before booking.

candidates.title: Chef & Winemaker Dinner: Harvest
candidates.summary: A collaborative chef-and-winemaker harvest dinner listed on Resy for Friday November 6, 2026, 5:30pm to 8:30pm, at City Winery's bistro on the Hudson River Park pier. The pairing lineup and per-person price were not shown on the listing.
candidates.fit: It is the one chef-plus-producer collab dinner I could pin to a Friday in the radar window. The pier location is more polished than secret, so it is a wife pick rather than a guys pick, and only if the winemaker turns out to be someone real.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge (closing weekend)
candidates.price_text: from about $49 on TodayTix; premium seats and couches run $135 to $348
candidates.summary: Company XIV's current mainstage show, a baroque-burlesque Little Red Riding Hood with circus, opera and aerial work, closes October 31. Final performances are Thu Oct 29 and Fri Oct 30 at 8pm, plus two shows on Halloween at 5pm and 10pm. Seating is by ticket tier, from single seats to champagne couches, with cocktail and champagne upgrades at the box office.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is his favorite room in the city and their Halloween burlesque was a highlight; this is the last chance at Petite Rouge before Nutcracker Rouge takes the stage, and the Halloween-night 10pm show is the most date-night version of it.

candidates.title: hABBAween
candidates.summary: An ABBA Halloween night at the Bell House on Friday Oct 30 at 8pm. It is listed on the Bell House calendar with tickets through Ticketmaster. Costumes are the whole point.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for an ABBA-themed dance night in the West Village and loved it; this is the same idea in a 400-cap Brooklyn room ten minutes from Fort Greene, on Halloween weekend.

candidates.title: Rocky Horror Picture Show with The Occasionalists
candidates.summary: The 12th annual Rocky Horror live-band karaoke Halloween extravaganza, with The Occasionalists playing the score while the room sings and heckles. Friday Oct 30, doors 7pm, show 7:30pm, 21+.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush; this is the participatory version with a live band in a 300-cap Gowanus room, which is squarely his format and an easy group-chat sell.

candidates.title: Kaiju Big Battel: Satan Sleeps Tonight
candidates.summary: Kaiju Big Battel is live costumed-monster pro wrestling, staged as a full narrative card with a crowd that yells at it. Sunday Nov 1 at 6pm at the Bell House.
candidates.fit: Live pro wrestling in a bar-sized room is exactly the weird programming he wants, and a 6pm Sunday start means he is home at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Wunderkammer: A Taxidermy Showcase and Competition
candidates.summary: A competitive taxidermy showcase at the Bell House on Thursday Oct 29 at 8pm, with entrants judged in front of a bar crowd. One of the venue's long-running oddball nights.
candidates.fit: This is the Thursday-night slot filled with something nobody in his group chat has heard of: a room full of rogue taxidermists competing while you drink. Pure word-of-mouth territory.

candidates.title: House of Hallucinations (Halloween)
candidates.summary: House of Yes's Halloween-night flagship: installations, aerial and performance pieces scattered through the building, and DJs on two floors. Doors 10pm Saturday Oct 31; announced performers include Ines Rau, Lingua Erotica live, Lauren Ritter and Sharlese. Costume is effectively mandatory.
candidates.fit: The one night a year House of Yes earns the trip: costumes, performance and a real dance floor rather than a bottle-service room. It is a late one, so file it under the occasional 2am exception.

candidates.title: Scary Good Comedy with Brittany Carney
candidates.summary: Comedians perform their full sets in Halloween costume and in character, hosted by Brittany Carney, with a lineup that includes Jenny Zigrino, Shaunak Godkhindi, Neel Ghosh and Don Will. There is an audience costume contest with prizes. Saturday Oct 31, doors 6:30pm, 21+.
candidates.fit: An early Halloween show he can dress up for, win something at, and still make a second stop afterward. Small room, working NYC comics, no arena-comedian energy.

candidates.title: Slipper Room Halloween Midnight Show
candidates.time_text: doors 10:45pm, shows at 11pm and 12:15am, dance party after
candidates.summary: The Slipper Room's late Halloween edition of its burlesque, sideshow and magic variety show, with two sets at 11pm and 12:15am and a dance party after. General admission $25, no drink minimums, at 167 Orchard Street.
candidates.fit: A 150-ish seat room that has been doing this since 1999, no drink minimum, cast announced day-of. Good second act after an early Brooklyn show if he's committing to a late Halloween.

candidates.title: Sup, Boo? with Alison Leiby and Josh Gondelman
candidates.summary: Alison Leiby and Josh Gondelman's long-running late show in the Union Hall basement, with Emmy Blotnick, Carson Olshansky and Anthony DeVito on this edition. Friday Oct 30 at 10pm.
candidates.fit: The Union Hall basement holds under 200 and the bill is all working New York comics, not touring headliners. A clean late-Friday option if Halloween costumes aren't the move.

candidates.title: A Drinking Game NYC: The Nightmare Before Christmas
candidates.summary: A Drinking Game stages a live, script-in-hand parody performance of The Nightmare Before Christmas with a drinking game running through it and audience participation. Saturday Oct 31 at 7pm at the Bell House.
candidates.fit: Interactive, costume-friendly, and done early enough on Halloween to roll into something else. Same register as the Rocky Horror night he already liked.

candidates.title: Dirty Circus: Halloween Edition
candidates.summary: House of Yes's longest-running variety show, told in three acts: circus, cabaret, burlesque, aerial, pole, drag and sideshow, with the lineup changing weekly. Halloween editions run Friday Oct 30 and Saturday Oct 31, doors 6:30pm, show 7:15pm. Seating is not guaranteed after 7:30pm, and tables can be booked.
candidates.fit: The seated, cocktail-in-hand version of House of Yes rather than the 2am version, which makes it a workable date night in the same lane as Company XIV.

candidates.title: Maggie's Scary Story Contest
candidates.summary: A dozen comics and writers, including George Civeris and Tim Mountain, compete telling scary stories in the Union Hall basement. Halloween afternoon, 5pm start.
candidates.fit: A 5pm Halloween show means he gets a real night out and is still free by 7. Competitive format, small basement, exactly the kind of show that only exists because someone's friends made it.

candidates.title: Don't Tell Manhattan: Hell's Kitchen (secret-location stand-up)
candidates.summary: Don't Tell Comedy's format: four to seven comics, lineup secret, venue a local business whose address is emailed to ticket holders at 8am the day of the show. This edition is Friday Oct 30 at 7pm in Hell's Kitchen.
candidates.fit: This is the closest bookable version of the random Midtown apartment comedy show he loved: no club, no drink minimum, you find out where you're going the morning of.

candidates.title: Gaydar: Halloween
candidates.summary: House of Yes's Halloween Gaydar night on Thursday Oct 29, doors 10pm: a headlining drag performance by Anania, a judged costume contest, host Amelia Montooth, and DJ sets from Ellen.J and TimaLikesMusic.
candidates.fit: Drag with a real crowd and a dance floor, the Bushwick equivalent of the Phoenix nights he does with friends. Thursday is his weeknight slot, though doors at 10pm make it a late one.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge
candidates.price_text: from about $35 Thu and Sun, from about $39 Fri and Sat
candidates.summary: Company XIV's burlesque-opera-circus rewrite of The Nutcracker opens Nov 12 and runs through Jan 30, 2027 at Théâtre XIV. Performances are Thursday through Saturday at 8pm and Sunday at 6pm, with the cast doubling as the venue's bartenders and servers. Entry-level seats start around $35.
candidates.fit: Two of his favorite things in one: Company XIV and the Nutcracker. Opening weeks and December Saturdays go first, so this is the book-now item of the month for a date night.

candidates.title: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker
candidates.time_text: evenings and matinees; opening night Nov 27
candidates.summary: New York City Ballet's annual run of Balanchine's Nutcracker at the David H. Koch Theater, Nov 27, 2026 through Jan 2, 2027, with a sensory-friendly performance on Jan 3. Full orchestra, School of American Ballet kids, Karinska costumes.
candidates.fit: His single favorite night in the city, and the good seats for December weekends are gone by mid-November. Book it this week and the December date night is handled.

candidates.title: Einstein on the Beach — 50th Anniversary Concert
candidates.summary: The Philip Glass Ensemble performs the concert arrangement of Glass and Wilson's Einstein on the Beach for its 50th anniversary, with an artistic installation by Es Devlin, conducted by Michael Riesman. Three nights, Nov 19 to 21, 7:30pm, at BAM's Howard Gilman Opera House. Tickets start at $65.
candidates.fit: Hypnotic, repetitive, built on arpeggios — it is the ancestor of everything he likes about a long melodic set, staged by Es Devlin, in his front yard. Three nights only and BAM members already have first crack.

candidates.title: Cold Plunge with Kurt Braunohler
candidates.summary: Kurt Braunohler's monthly Union Hall show, with Emmy Blotnick, Ahamed Weinberg and Nonye Brown-West on the Nov 4 edition. 7:30pm in the basement.
candidates.fit: Braunohler is a real headliner in an under-200 basement, and the name is a bonus given how much time he spends in a plunge tub. Wednesday, so only worth it because the bill is this good.

candidates.title: Sam Tallent
candidates.summary: Comedian and novelist Sam Tallent headlines the Bell House on Thursday Nov 5 at 7:30pm, booked through the venue's Ticketmaster page.
candidates.fit: A Thursday headliner in a Brooklyn music room rather than a comedy club, with no two-drink minimum and no arena seating. Easy walk-up plan for two or three of the guys.

candidates.title: Moshe Kasher: Coda/Switch
candidates.summary: Moshe Kasher brings his show Coda/Switch to the Bell House on Sunday Nov 8 at 7:30pm.
candidates.fit: Kasher's material lives in Jewish identity and deaf-culture storytelling, which lines up with his interest in Jewish cultural programming, and the Bell House keeps it to a few hundred people instead of a theater.

candidates.title: NYC's Halloween Punderdome: Pun and Pun-Costume Compuntitions
candidates.summary: Punderdome is a live pun competition judged by audience applause, hosted by Firestone, with returning champs and a costume category for the Halloween edition. Wednesday Oct 28, doors 7pm, show 8pm, 21+. Audience members can get pulled in to compete.
candidates.fit: Interactive, cult-following, no marketing budget, and you can end up on stage. It's a Wednesday, so only worth it if he wants the one plan nobody else in the group has heard of.

candidates.title: Eddie Pepitone at Union Hall
candidates.summary: Eddie Pepitone headlines two late shows at Union Hall, Nov 10 and Nov 11, both at 10pm, during the week Union Hall is also running New York Comedy Festival editions of its regular shows.
candidates.fit: A genuinely great club comic in a basement that holds under 200, at 10pm, which is as close as stand-up gets to his small-room sweet spot.

candidates.title: Neel Ghosh: Pagol
candidates.summary: Neel Ghosh's hour at Union Hall on Friday Nov 13 at 10pm, with Nimesh Patel, Sureni Weerasekera, Zubi Ahmed, Sabeen Sadiq and Misha Han on the bill.
candidates.fit: A stacked guest list for a basement show — Nimesh Patel plays theaters now — and the kind of lineup you only catch because you read the venue calendar rather than a listicle.

candidates.title: La Distance
candidates.time_text: evening performances; check calendar for matinees
candidates.summary: Tiago Rodrigues's La Distance, part of BAM's Next Wave 2026, runs Nov 18 to 29: a father on Earth and a daughter who has emigrated to Mars, performed in French with English titles.
candidates.fit: Rodrigues is a BAM regular and this is the opposite of generic theater; it's a five-minute walk from his door and pairs with the Einstein weekend if he wants a proper Next Wave run.

candidates.title: The Tiny Cupboard nightly stand-up
candidates.summary: An indie comedy club in a Bushwick house with a rooftop, running stand-up nearly every night plus free karaoke, with lineups of local pros and drop-ins. Tickets typically run $5 to $10 with no drink minimum.
candidates.fit: The default fallback when a Thursday opens up at short notice: under 50 seats, ten dollars, and nobody's tourist map points there.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Museum First Saturday
candidates.summary: The museum's free monthly after-hours party: DJs, dancing, films, talks, art-making and a pop-up market across the building, with galleries open late. Nov 7 is the first Saturday of the month; the specific November lineup was not posted at the time of writing.
candidates.fit: A museum that turns into a party, in Prospect Heights, free, and over by 10. Worth checking the lineup midweek — past editions have had DJs playing dancehall, afrobeats and amapiano, which is his current lane.

candidates.title: World Spa full-day banya session
candidates.time_text: Sun to Thu 10am to 10pm, Fri and Sat 9am to 11pm; free Aufguss ceremonies at 12pm, 2pm, 4pm and 6pm in the Event Sauna, herbal steam ritual at 1pm, 3pm and 5pm in the Grand Banya
candidates.summary: World Spa is the big Brooklyn bathhouse in Borough Park: 16 thermal rooms, hammams, onsen pools, a Grand Banya and a restaurant you can eat in between rounds. Day passes start at $99 and the Aufguss towel ceremonies (12pm, 2pm, 4pm, 6pm) are included with admission, with the oak-leaf herbal steam ritual running at 1pm, 3pm and 5pm. Open until 11pm on Friday and Saturday, so you can make it an all-day thing.
candidates.fit: The full day at the Russian bathhouse with a friend is one of his favorite things he's done in the city; this is the bigger, newer, more serious version of that, and it's a Brooklyn trip rather than a Manhattan one. Free Aufguss four times a day gives the day structure instead of just sitting in heat.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Ave
candidates.summary: Bathhouse has opened a third New York location on Atlantic Avenue, alongside Williamsburg and Flatiron, with the same hot/cold format: saunas, steam, cold plunges, pools, scrubs and massage, plus daily Aufguss ceremonies. Booking runs through their own system at bathhouseatlanticave.try.be. Their site also lists a rooftop pool page for NYC, which I could not confirm is at this location.
candidates.fit: It is the closest real bathhouse to Fort Greene he can basically walk or take one stop to, which makes a Thursday night plunge with a friend an actual plan rather than a trek. New enough that most people in his group chat haven't been yet.

candidates.title: Aufguss sauna ceremony at Bathhouse Williamsburg
candidates.summary: Bathhouse runs Aufguss ceremonies daily at every location, seven slots a day from noon to 9pm, where a sauna master pours on the stones and whips the heat around the room with towels. You book a day pass and time your visit to land on a ceremony. The 9pm slot works as a late Thursday.
candidates.fit: He trains Muay Thai in Williamsburg, so this is a same-neighborhood post-training move: train, sweat, plunge, done. Aufguss is the participatory version of a sauna rather than sitting there staring at a sand timer, which is the kind of thing he actually wants.

candidates.title: Watch the 50th TCS New York City Marathon from Lafayette Avenue
candidates.time_text: lead runners hit Brooklyn mid-morning after the 8am start and the staggered 9:40am to 11am waves; the Fort Greene and Clinton Hill stretch is busiest late morning into early afternoon
candidates.summary: The marathon runs Sunday November 1, 2026, the 50th running, with an 8:00am start and staggered waves to 11am. The course leaves Fourth Avenue and runs east along Lafayette Avenue through Fort Greene and Clinton Hill around miles 8 and 9, which is the loudest stretch of the whole course. Free, no ticket, just walk out the door.
candidates.fit: This is literally his front yard, it is the 50th edition, and it is the one morning a year when Fort Greene turns into a stadium. Stroller-friendly, over by early afternoon, and the one-year-old gets a wall of noise and a brass band without anyone having to sit still.

candidates.title: F1 2026 Mexican Grand Prix screening at Classic Car Club
candidates.summary: Classic Car Club's new Midtown clubhouse screens the 2026 F1 season live in a dedicated screening room, with overflow screens in the bar and restaurant. The Mexican Grand Prix goes up Sunday November 1 at 3pm; Brazil follows November 8 at noon and Las Vegas on November 21 at 11pm. Screening-room tickets are sold separately from bar reservations.
candidates.fit: A car club's screening room with people who actually build cars is a very different room from a sports bar, and it's the Sunday-afternoon slot that works for him. Pairs with the marathon that morning if he wants a full day.

candidates.title: QC NY spa day on Governors Island
candidates.summary: QC NY is the Italian-run spa in the old officers' houses on Governors Island: heated outdoor courtyard pools, timber saunas, steam rooms, foot baths and over 20 wellness stations, with food and wine included in the admission tiers. Their current site is pushing the autumn version, outdoor fires and heated pools with the skyline going dark early. You get there by ferry; prices are on their admissions page.
candidates.fit: A ferry with an actual destination plus a sauna and plunge circuit, which is two of his things in one afternoon. Sitting in a heated outdoor pool in November looking back at Lower Manhattan is a date night his wife will rate higher than another restaurant.

candidates.title: TWA Hotel rooftop infinity pool and observation deck
candidates.summary: The heated rooftop infinity pool and observation deck at the TWA Hotel stay open 365 days a year, with the Pool Bar alongside, looking straight down the runway. Day passes are sold through the hotel; current pricing was not confirmed. It's the Saarinen terminal, so the building is half the point.
candidates.fit: He has already done this once and loved it; the cold-weather version, steam coming off the water while 777s rotate in front of you, is the better one. Works as a weird weekend-daytime move with the guys or as a strange date.

candidates.title: Othership Williamsburg guided sauna and ice bath
candidates.summary: Othership's Williamsburg room runs guided hot-and-cold classes, a large Western red cedar sauna, private ice baths and a commons area, booked class by class through their schedule page. They also sell drop-in passes and run occasional themed nights. Their listed New York event for this week is a singles night at the Flatiron location on October 30.
candidates.fit: The guided format is the interactive version of a plunge, a facilitator running rounds instead of you staring at a clock, and it's a short walk from where he trains. Skip the Tinder singles social on the 30th, that one is not for him.

candidates.title: Russian and Turkish Baths, East Village
candidates.summary: The 1892 banya on East 10th Street: Russian room, redwood sauna, steam, ice-cold plunge pool, platza oak-leaf beatings, and a restaurant upstairs where you eat in a robe. Admission and hours are on their hours page; current pricing was not confirmed. Cash-era vibes, no spa music.
candidates.fit: This is the room where he already had one of his best days in the city. November is when it is actually good, and platza with a friend is the interactive version rather than just sitting in heat.

candidates.title: Daikoku NYC meets and events
candidates.summary: Daikoku NYC is the nonprofit JDM and USDM car group behind curated meets, parades and gallery collaborations around the city; recent ones include a Main Street parade in Flushing and a fundraiser night at Car Part Time. Their events page lists public, registration-required and approval-required gatherings. I could not confirm a specific dated event inside this window.
candidates.fit: He named Daikoku NYC himself as the scene he wants deeper into; the move is to watch their events page and the next public meet rather than wait for a listicle to cover it. Registration-required and approval-only is exactly the format he likes.

candidates.title: Hotel pool and spa day passes via ResortPass New York
candidates.summary: ResortPass sells single-day access to New York hotel pools, spas and fitness facilities without booking a room, with inventory changing by season. Winter inventory skews to indoor and heated pools and hotel spas. I was not able to load the page to confirm which hotels and what prices are live right now.
candidates.fit: The TWA pool day is the template; this is how he finds the next one. Worth a scan when the weather is bad and he still wants a plan that involves water.

candidates.title: Ruth Rehmann's 'Illusions': Rob Madole and Megan Nolan in Conversation
candidates.price_text: not published on the calendar listing
candidates.summary: Goethe-Institut New York's calendar lists a Thursday, November 19 reading and panel, 6:30pm to 8pm, on Ruth Rehmann's postwar novel 'Illusions', with translator Rob Madole and novelist Megan Nolan. In the Goethe library space at 30 Irving Place.
candidates.fit: Thursday night, German postwar literature, and Megan Nolan is a sharp enough interlocutor that it won't be a dry academic panel. Pairs with dinner nearby.

candidates.title: America's Liberal Reckoning: A Munk Debate at 92NY (Fareed Zakaria vs. Patrick Deneen)
candidates.time_text: evening; start time not listed on either organizer page I could read
candidates.price_text: not published on the pages I could read
candidates.summary: The Munk Debates come to New York for the first time, co-hosted with 92NY on Thursday, November 12, days after the midterms. Fareed Zakaria argues against the motion that liberalism has failed America, Notre Dame political philosopher Patrick Deneen argues for it, Rudyard Griffiths moderates. Both the Munk Debates site and 92NY's season page list the same date and venue.
candidates.fit: This is the 'only when the speaker is a real draw' bar cleared: Zakaria against Deneen is the single highest-caliber ideas night in the window, it is a Thursday, and it is a format where the room actually votes rather than claps.

candidates.title: Rella's 15th Annual Laternenlauf (St. Martin's Lantern Walk)
candidates.price_text: suggested donation $10 per child, $5 per adult, cash only; lanterns $15, electric candles $2
candidates.summary: Rella's Spielhaus, the German-American family outfit in New York, runs its 15th annual lantern walk in Central Park on Sunday, November 8, 5pm to 6:30pm, starting at the Tarr Family Playground. Musicians lead the traditional Laternen songs, there is a telling of the St. Martin story, a procession, and hot chocolate at the end. RSVP requested, cash only, lanterns sold on site.
candidates.fit: He already plays Lichterkinder lantern songs to the 1-year-old. This is the actual tradition those songs come from, run by the German-speaking community rather than staged for tourists, and a stroller-and-carrier walk in the park is about the right length for a toddler.

candidates.title: Volkmar and Margret Sander Prize 2026: Johannes von Moltke
candidates.price_text: not published on the calendar listing
candidates.summary: Deutsches Haus at NYU awards its Sander Prize to film and cultural historian Johannes von Moltke on Friday, November 6, 6pm to 8pm, at 42 Washington Mews. Prize evenings at Deutsches Haus are a talk plus a reception in a room that holds well under a hundred people.
candidates.fit: Friday evening, German intellectual scene, tiny room, and a reception where you end up talking to the speaker. The opposite of a listicle event.

candidates.title: Tammam Azzam: A Horizon Remains
candidates.summary: The first New York solo show and first US institutional presentation of Syrian-German artist Tammam Azzam, at the Goethe-Institut, running September 5 to November 15, 2026. Listed as free on the Goethe-Institut's events page.
candidates.fit: Free, ten minutes from the Union Square end of his usual Manhattan orbit, and the kind of thing he can stack onto the Goethe film night on the 29th rather than making a separate trip.

candidates.title: Germany and the Nuclear Question: Energy Security After the Phase-Out
candidates.venue: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy
candidates.price_text: free (CGEP events are free; registration required)
candidates.summary: Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy has this on its 'Coming Up' list for Tuesday, November 10, 1pm to 2pm, on German energy security after the nuclear phase-out. No physical venue is given on the events index, which usually means it is a webinar.
candidates.fit: German energy policy plus European energy security is the exact intersection of two of his interests, and CGEP is one of the few places where the panel is actual market people. Midday on a Tuesday, so this is a listen-at-your-desk item, not a night out.

candidates.title: Neue Galerie First Fridays (November)
candidates.summary: The German Events NYC calendar lists Neue Galerie's monthly First Fridays for November 2026, falling on Friday, November 6. Neue Galerie is the German and Austrian art museum on Fifth Avenue with Cafe Sabarsky downstairs. I could not open the museum's own page to confirm the hours or the admission policy for that evening.
candidates.fit: A date-night version of his German interest: Klimt and Schiele upstairs, Viennese cafe downstairs, no line culture. Worth one check of the museum's own page before committing.

candidates.title: Grand Army Plaza Greenmarket
candidates.time_text: Saturday morning into the early afternoon; confirm exact hours with GrowNYC
candidates.address: Prospect Park West at Flatbush Avenue
candidates.summary: The Prospect Park Alliance events feed lists the Saturday Greenmarket at Grand Army Plaza, at the park's north entrance. It is the biggest year-round farmers market in Brooklyn, running every Saturday, and it is a short walk or a short ride from Fort Greene.
candidates.fit: A low-effort Saturday morning with the 1-year-old that is still somewhere, not a playground: apple cider, a bakery stand, and a walk into Prospect Park afterwards. Use it as the backup when nothing better lands on a Saturday.

candidates.title: German-Language Sunday Service and Kaffeestunde at St. Paul's
candidates.time_text: Sunday morning; exact time not confirmed
candidates.summary: The German Events NYC calendar lists the German-language Sunday service and community coffee hour at St. Paul's German church in Chelsea on Sunday, November 1. This is the oldest German-speaking congregation community gathering in Manhattan; the coffee hour afterwards is where the German-speaking families actually are.
candidates.fit: The point here is the Kaffeestunde, not the sermon: it is the German-speaking community in one room, and it is how you find out about the Nikolaus and Christmas events before they are posted. Fair warning if church is not his thing.

candidates.title: Governors Island ferry day
candidates.time_text: daytime; ferry schedule varies by season
candidates.price_text: not verified for the current season
candidates.summary: Governors Island is open year-round with ferries from Brooklyn Bridge Park's Pier 6 as well as Lower Manhattan. Off-season it is nearly empty, which is the best version of it. I could not load the island's own page to confirm the current ferry schedule or fares, so check before leaving the house.
candidates.fit: His 'ferry ride with a destination' category, and the Pier 6 boat is the easy one from Fort Greene. Carrier-friendly, flat, done by mid-afternoon, and the boat itself is the entertainment for a 1-year-old.

candidates.title: CircoLoco New York — Night 3 (Teksupport)
candidates.summary: Teksupport closes its three-day Circoloco Halloween run with a Sunday session at Brooklyn Storehouse: Dixon, Bedouin, Chloé Caillet, Jimi Jules, Prospa, Dean Turnley, Miguelle & Tons and Rossi. Doors at noon, done by midnight, 21+. Final tickets were being pushed on DICE and RA as of this week.
candidates.fit: This is the Kx5-scale warehouse night he gets a few times a year, except it runs in daylight and ends at midnight — a dad-compatible version of the big room. Dixon and Jimi Jules are squarely in the melodic-house lane he lives in.

candidates.title: Elsewhere Halloween: Major League DJz, Bantu, SAIDAH, D Stone, Kush Jones
candidates.summary: Elsewhere's Halloween night pairs amapiano architects Major League DJz with garage and house selectors SAIDAH and D Stone plus Kush Jones across the building. Tickets from about $47 on DICE; the venue flagged it as close to selling out.
candidates.fit: Amapiano and Afro-house are his current phase, and Major League DJz are the headline act of that scene — on Halloween, in a room where you can still see the booth. Costume night, no bottle service.

candidates.title: Dope Jams Halloween Ball — Turtle Bugg, 4AM NYC, GE-OLOGY
candidates.summary: Paul Nickerson's Dope Jams record-shop crew takes over Public Records' Sound Room for its annual Halloween Ball, with Turtle Bugg, 4AM NYC and GE-OLOGY. Costumes are the point; the Sound Room is a small, serious hi-fi space, doors around 11pm.
candidates.fit: Exactly the kind of thing that never makes a listicle: a record store's annual party in a 150-ish capacity sound room, fifteen minutes from Fort Greene. Costume night with the guys, good sound, no line culture.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge — final performances
candidates.time_text: evening performances, check the night you pick
candidates.summary: Company XIV's Little Red Riding Hood burlesque closes Halloween night; the company says only a handful of performances remain. Add-ons include champagne service and tarot readings before the show.
candidates.fit: He already rates Company XIV's Halloween run as one of his best nights out — this is the last weekend of this one, and it's the obvious babysitter night with his wife.

candidates.title: Unsound New York: Mark Broom, Julia Govor / Blue Hour, Neel / Yasmeenah
candidates.price_text: from $24 (tiers up to about $27, incl. fees)
candidates.summary: Public Records' Friday as posted by the venue: a UK/Russia/Italy techno bill with Mark Broom, Julia Govor, Blue Hour, Neel and Yasmeenah, alongside Unsound New York listening sessions earlier in the evening (Jim O'Rourke and Eiko Ishibashi; a talk with Emily Witt).
candidates.fit: Proper European techno in a 200-cap sound room a few subway stops from home, on his main weekend-night slot. Blue Hour and Neel are the melodic-to-hypnotic end he actually listens to, not festival EDM.

candidates.title: Halloween at All Night Skate with Mom and the Fam
candidates.time_text: night, costume contest during the show
candidates.summary: The All Night Skate Halloween party with performers The Opulent Doll and Junior Mintt, DJs Sadboy and Danny Waits, a costume contest and Malört shots, announced by host Pam on Instagram.
candidates.fit: He's already been to All Night Skate and liked it; this is that bar doing its weirdest night of the year with drag performers and a costume contest. Small room, cheap, five minutes from the Bushwick spots he likes.

candidates.title: Halloween at Threes Brewing Greenpoint — family day, then Form & Phantom
candidates.time_text: 12pm to 7pm family trick-or-treating and costume contest; DJs from 9pm, 21+
candidates.summary: Threes runs Halloween in two halves: noon to 7pm is all-ages with trick-or-treating and a costume contest (winner gets a $50 gift card, announced at 7pm), then Brooklyn DJ collective Form & Phantom takes the room from 9pm, free entry, 21+.
candidates.fit: One address covers the family pick and the night out: toddler in costume in a brewery at 2pm, then come back without him. Beer-yard hang with a reason to be there, which is his format.

candidates.title: 12th Annual Barnacle Parade
candidates.time_text: evening, gathers around Van Brunt and Pioneer
candidates.summary: Red Hook's homemade sea-creature parade marks the anniversary of Superstorm Sandy every October 29, organized by neighbors rather than any institution. Strong Rope brewed this year's Barnacle King Golden Ale with Keg & Lantern and Sixpoint, with proceeds going to Red Hook Mutual Aid.
candidates.fit: Red Hook, Strong Rope, a neighborhood thing with no marketing budget, on a Thursday — and a stroller-friendly 20 minutes before the beer part. Exact opposite of the Village Halloween Parade.

candidates.title: German Zombie Films: EVER AFTER + second feature
candidates.summary: A Halloween-week German zombie double feature at the Goethe-Institut, including Carolina Hellsgård's EVER AFTER, introduced by film curator and critic Deniz Sertkol. Free, but registration is required.
candidates.fit: German-language film, free, on his Thursday slot, in a room of maybe eighty people — the German-culture lane he keeps asking for, with a Halloween excuse attached.

candidates.title: WISHMASTER on 35mm (Ridiculous <> Sublime)
candidates.summary: Nitehawk screens Robert Kurtzman's 1997 practical-effects horror WISHMASTER on 35mm as part of its Ridiculous <> Sublime series, Thursday at the Prospect Park theater, with full food and drink service at your seat.
candidates.fit: A cheap, loud Thursday with one or two friends: 35mm print, beers at the seat, ten minutes from Fort Greene. Nitehawk's repertory series is the kind of programming you only find by reading the calendar.

candidates.title: Halloween Comedy in Character + audience costume contest
candidates.summary: Littlefield's Halloween show: comedians perform their entire sets in costume and in character, hosted by Brittany Carney with Jenny Zigrino, Neel Ghost, Don Will and others. There's an audience costume contest with prizes.
candidates.fit: Early enough to do before a party, small enough to talk to the bartender, and he has to actually show up in costume — the participation angle he likes.

candidates.title: Halloween Bingo with Sinclair Ariel
candidates.summary: Drag bingo at Phoenix on Halloween night at 6pm hosted by Sinclair Ariel, per the bar's Instagram. Dive-bar pricing, no cover announced.
candidates.fit: He already does drag nights at Phoenix with the guys; this is the same bar with a bingo card in your hand at an hour that still leaves the night open.

candidates.title: Cantos al Viento Halloween family concert
candidates.summary: The Spanish-language kids' music project Cantos al Viento plays a costumed Halloween afternoon show at Barbès, Saturday at 4pm. Barbès is a 50-seat back room with a pass-the-hat tradition.
candidates.fit: A kids' concert in an actual music venue, not a playground — and Barbès is a room he'd want to be in anyway. Costumes, done well before dinner, toddler-scale.

candidates.title: Conducta b2b AceMo, Surusinghe, x3butterfly b2b Physical Therapy
candidates.summary: Public Records' Sunday after Halloween: UK garage producer Conducta back to back with New York's AceMo, plus Surusinghe and x3butterfly b2b Physical Therapy, listed on DICE from about $24.
candidates.fit: A Sunday recovery option in the Sound Room if Saturday was too much — garage and house with no 2am requirement, and cheap enough to decide same-day.

candidates.title: B3K Invites NY: Brutalismus 3000, SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera, Nurse
candidates.time_text: doors in the evening, late night
candidates.summary: Berlin duo Brutalismus 3000 headline a special edition of RUSH at Knockdown Center on Friday, November 6, with SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera and Nurse (Body Bag). Tickets went on general sale in October via RA.
candidates.fit: Berlin techno in its most obnoxious, fun form, in the Knockdown main hall — the German lane and the big-room lane in one night. Book it now; SPFDJ bills there have been selling out.

candidates.title: GERMAN PUNK: rarely screened films from the German punk era
candidates.time_text: evening screenings, first film at 6:45pm on the opening night
candidates.summary: The German Film Office and Goethe-Institut bring a week of films shot in West and East Germany between 1979 and 1999 documenting the punk scene, including Super-8 shorts scored by Einstürzende Neubauten and Malaria!. German punk figure Gudrun Gut introduces EINSTÜRZENDE NEUBAUTEN: LIEBESLIEDER on November 6.
candidates.fit: Deep German cultural programming with no marketing behind it — rare prints, a Berlin scene legend in the room. The Gut introduction clashes with Brutalismus 3000 the same night, so pick one.

candidates.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack and the Invention of the German Underground
candidates.summary: The first exhibition outside Germany devoted to Alfred Hilsberg and the ZickZack label: rare records, badges, flyers and posters from Christian Iffland's collection plus Sabine Schwabroh's photography. Produced with the Goethe-Institut, free, on view through November 7.
candidates.fit: A small free gallery show about the label that invented the German underground — exactly the Berlin-adjacent rabbit hole he likes, and a 30-minute stop before dinner in Manhattan.

candidates.title: Butcher's Mouth one-year anniversary party
candidates.summary: Butcher's Mouth marks its first year with a party at The Tiny Cupboard in collaboration with The Fox and King: DJs Bojaq, Prod Merciless and Hotline Castle, burlesque from India Jenell and Kobrada Don, handmade goods and games. RSVP link in the organizer's bio.
candidates.fit: A tiny independent collective throwing its own birthday in a Bushwick walk-up venue, early enough to be home by midnight. This is the 'had to know someone' end of the scene.

candidates.title: New York Emos x Grrrl Afraid mixtape night
candidates.summary: New York Emos and Grrrl Afraid burn physical CDs of your submitted playlist at All Night Skate; you decorate the sleeve and trade with strangers while the room plays 2000s emo. Free with RSVP, playlists submitted in advance.
candidates.fit: 2000s emo, a bar he already likes, and you actually make something rather than watch — the interactive format he rates, on a Thursday.

candidates.title: Dialogue and Discourse: Jewish Patronage of the Wiener Werkstätte
candidates.summary: Elana Shapira (University of Applied Arts Vienna) and Lisa Silverman (UW-Milwaukee) trace how Jewish patrons funded and shaped the Vienna workshop, one of two closing programs for the museum's Wiener Werkstätte exhibition, which comes down November 15.
candidates.fit: Serious academic speakers in a small auditorium on a Thursday, and it doubles as a reason to see the exhibition before it closes — his Jewish-culture lane done at talk level, not festival level.

laneReports.notes:
Fetch budget ran out partway through, so some items lean on secondary listings. What I read directly and can stand behind: the Good Room calendar (goodroombk.com), the Elsewhere calendar (elsewhere.club/events), the RA New York City listing page, and the RA event page for 2ManyDJs. Those are marked verified.

What failed or was unreliable: knockdown.center would not load at all (both /upcoming/ and /events), so every Knockdown item here is sourced from Bandsintown, AXS, Crowdvolt and Songkick rather than the venue — confirm door times and face-value prices before buying, especially DJ Harvey (Nov 13) and Dax J (Nov 14). The Avant Gardner events page returned a cached 2025 calendar; Bandsintown lists Miss Monique (Nov 13) and Madeon (Nov 14) at the Brooklyn Mirage, but the Mirage is an outdoor summer room and I could not confirm whether those are actually in the Great Hall, so I left them out. Public Records' events page would not resolve (only the marketing homepage loaded), and Nowadays only publishes through its RA club page, so nothing from Public Records is included this week. Teksupport's own site blocked fetching; note that RA reported a court ordering Teksupport and its parent to cease operations after November 7, which is why CircoLoco at Brooklyn Storehouse this weekend may be one of the last of these — treat that as reported, not confirmed by me.

CircoLoco pricing is resale-only in what I could see ($197 to $364 incl. fees depending on night); I could not confirm face value, and AXS/StubHub both showed very low inventory. The Xanadu WITCHSLAP night (skate + Choke Hole drag wrestling + dance party) came only from the RA city listing; I could not open the event page for door time, price or address, so it is flagged unverified despite being the single best thematic match this week.

Thin lanes: no German or Berlin artist is touring New York inside either window — Kalkbrenner has no US dates, Deichkind, K.I.Z and Ski Aggu are all playing Europe. The Berlin angle this week is Herrensauna at BASEMENT and Brutalismus 3000 at Knockdown instead. I also could not get to Brooklyn Paramount, Kings Theatre, Brooklyn Bowl (emo/2000s nights), Under the K Bridge, The Lot Radio or Brooklyn Steel's hip-hop bookings before the budget ran out, so the hip-hop / 2000s New York rap lane and the themed-dance-night lane are both underfed this week.

Honest accounting of this lane. Verified by reading the organizers' own pages: the full UFC schedule (ufc.com/events) and the UFC 334 event page, the Barclays Center events calendar, and the Prudential Center events calendar. Everything marked 'verified' came from one of those. Knicks dates are marked 'likely' because I could only confirm them on the official Knicks Ticketmaster schedule page and CBS Sports, not an arena page I opened directly. What failed: msg.com/calendar renders its event list in JavaScript and returned zero events, so I could not sweep the Garden and the Infosys Theater (formerly Hulu Theater) for boxing or kickboxing cards. BoxingScene's schedule page returned stale data from May 2026. kingscombat.com is now a parked GoDaddy domain for sale, so I could not confirm anything from his gym; the Williamsburg location itself is still listed as operating at 219 South 3rd St. churchboxing.com is a boxing club in Maldon, England, not the Manhattan gym, and I ran out of fetch budget before I could find the correct Church Street Boxing URL. What is genuinely missing and should be chased next week: (1) boxing at the Infosys Theater at MSG. Straight answer: my web tool budget was cut off partway through this lane, and that is why this list is shorter and thinner than it should be. What happened: web_fetch was blocked on several trusted sources outright (Eater NY returned url_not_allowed; resy.com/events and punchdrink.com would not load), and then the whole search/fetch quota hit its ceiling about fifteen calls in. Only ONE item here is fully verified against the organizer's own page: Other Half's Stout Season on December 5, which I read end to end (date, 12-4pm, Centre Street, 40+ breweries, Eventbrite link) — but even there the ticket price lives on Eventbrite, which I never got to open. RAW WINE New York (Nov 8-9, Industry City) is 'likely': the organizer's own page text and the Industry City listing both show the same dates and hours, but I read them through search results, not a direct fetch, and I have no ticket price. Everything marked unverified came from a single source and needs a phone call or a page check before it goes in the email: the Resy items (Badshah, SSAW, City Winery, Jacob's Pickles) came off Resy's city events index, which renders as a jumbled block of names and timestamps, so the name-to-date mapping is my best read and nothing more; the two Halloween bar items came from one RoamRecs guide updated four days ago and I could not confirm Desert 5 Spot's address or borough at all, which is why its borough is 'Other'. Maccabee Bar and Choke Hole are deliberately dateless radar alerts, not picks — both are annual, both are squarely his taste, neither has announced 2026 dates that I could find. What I never got to, and what the next pass should hit first: Strong Rope's events calendar (their page lists food pop-ups and Red Hook taproom nights through the fall but I only saw October entries), Threes Brewing, KCBC, Radegast Hall, Sunken Harbor Club's special nights, Tock New York, The Infatuation and Grub Street openings, All Night Skate's upcoming dates, live-wrestling-in-a-bar nights, Beaujolais Nouveau night (third Thursday, Nov 19) at Brooklyn wine bars, Thanksgiving-eve bar nights and Friendsgiving group dinners, and the big shared-table category entirely — I found zero verified whole-animal dinners, Korean BBQ or banquet nights for a group of guys this round, which is a real gap. Also worth chasing: The Lineup, a one-night sous-chef pop-up series that runs five courses with five wines at the Food52 offices in Brooklyn; it is exactly his register but I could not find a confirmed 2026 date. Nothing in this list is invented; where I did not have a fact I left the field empty rather than guess.

Budget problems: the web_fetch tool hit its usage ceiling early, so after the first round I could only confirm things through web_search results. Directly fetched and read in full: companyxiv.com, unionhallny.com, littlefieldnyc.com, thebellhouseny.com — everything sourced from those four is solid on date, time and venue. Items marked verified beyond those four were confirmed from the organizer's or ticketer's own page content returned in search (calendar.houseofyes.org, slipperroom.com, bam.org, nycballet.com, todaytix.com).

Prices are the big gap. The Bell House sells through Ticketmaster and Union Hall through Eventbrite, and I could not open those checkout pages to read actual prices, so price_text is empty for hABBAween, Kaiju Big Battel, Wunderkammer, A Drinking Game, Sam Tallent, Moshe Kasher and all the Union Hall shows. Littlefield prices likewise unread. Historically these rooms are $15 to $30, but I am not going to print a number I did not see. Tell him to expect that range and check at checkout.

Could not verify at all, so left out: Nitehawk Cinema and Alamo Drafthouse Brooklyn themed/costume screenings for Halloween week (their calendars would not load and search returned nothing dated for Oct 2026); Kings Theatre; Brooklyn Comedy Collective's current schedule; the Brooklyn Botanic Garden Lightscape 2026 opening date and on-sale, which should be chased next week since it normally opens in mid-to-late November; and any Don't Tell Comedy show in Brooklyn — the only dated one I could find in the window was the Hell's Kitchen show on Oct 30, and their Brooklyn neighborhood editions (Bed-Stuy, Park Slope, Williamsburg) post on short notice, so it's worth re-checking donttellcomedy.com midweek.

The Brooklyn Museum First Saturday entry is the weakest item here: Nov 7 is the first Saturday and the series runs monthly, but the museum had not posted a November 2026 lineup page I could read, so it is flagged unverified and the URL is the general programs page rather than an event page.

One scheduling note for the email: Oct 30 and Oct 31 are badly overbooked — hABBAween, Rocky Horror at Littlefield, House of Hallucinations, Dirty Circus, Scary Good Comedy, the Slipper Room midnight show and the last Petite Rouge performances all collide. Petite Rouge closing on Oct 31 is the one that disappears permanently.

Honest accounting: my web_fetch and web_search budget ran out partway through this lane, so the coverage is uneven. Verified by actually reading the organizer page: Bathhouse (bathhouse.com, including the daily Aufguss schedule and the fact that there is now a third NYC location on Atlantic Ave), Othership (events page shows only three listings, two at the Toronto Yorkville location and a Tinder singles social at Flatiron on Oct 30, so nothing NYC-specific worth his time this week), World Spa (hours, $99-plus day passes, free Aufguss at 12/2/4/6 and herbal steam ritual at 1/3/5), QC NY, the TWA Hotel pool page, and Bike New York's events page. Not verified, loaded only as search-surfaced page content: the NYRR marathon pages, the Classic Car Club calendar (ccccal.com and apply.classiccarclubmanhattan.com), and Daikoku NYC. What I could NOT load at all and should be re-checked next week: transalt.org/events, nyrr.org/run/races (full race calendar), the Daikoku NYC events page itself, ccccal.com directly, resortpass.com, and janemotorcycles.com. Two dead ends worth recording: Union Garage has closed its Brooklyn store and moved to Bridgeport, Connecticut, so drop it from the trusted-source list; and Bike New York has nothing local on the calendar right now, with the 2026 Twin Lights Ride cancelled for weather and the Discover Hudson Valley Ride not running in 2026. The Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K on Oct 31 is sold out across every registration option, so it is not a pick. Gaps I did not get to fill: organized group bike rides this weekend, bouldering comps, open mats, Rockaway or Riis in-season items (off-season now anyway), and any Halloween-weekend sauna or plunge party. Prices are left blank wherever I could not read a real number rather than guessed. The Five Boro Bike Tour sits outside both windows as an event but registration is open now and it sells out, which is why it is in here.

Big caveat on method: the fetch tool stopped working after about ten page loads, so most of what is above was confirmed by reading organizer page content returned through search rather than by opening the page myself. I marked only two items 'verified' (Rella's Laternenlauf and the Munk Debate at 92NY) because for those I had the organizer's full page text with matching date, venue and, for Rella's, price. Everything marked 'likely' came from the organizer's own events calendar (Goethe-Institut, Deutsches Haus at NYU, Columbia CGEP) but without the event detail page, so prices are mostly unconfirmed.

What is thin, and it is a real gap: the Jewish lane. I could not load 92NY's main events calendar, The Jewish Museum, Museum of Jewish Heritage, Center for Jewish History, or the Folksbiene past the homepage, and I could not load Barbes' calendar at all. Barbes publishes its month as a PDF rather than a web calendar, so the Sunday klezmer and Slavic Soul Party style bookings could not be confirmed for this window. Folksbiene's current season does include 'New York Sings Yiddish' and a Yiddish 'Pirates of Penzance' (Di Yam Gazlonim), but no dates were readable, so I left them out rather than guess. Same for the Maccabee Bar Hanukkah pop-up: Hanukkah falls in early December 2026, so it belongs on the radar, but I found no 2026 announcement I could cite. Next week this lane needs a dedicated pass at nytf.org, thejewishmuseum.org and the Barbes PDF.

Creative scene: nothing verified. Gowanus Open Studios and Bushwick Open Studios both run earlier in the fall, and I found no zine or art book fair with a confirmed date in either window. Not reported rather than invented.

Ideas: the Council on Foreign Relations events page only served its past-events archive (most recent, October 23, a conversation with Kuwait Petroleum Corporation's CEO), and CFR's on-site meetings are largely members-only anyway. Asia Society, Carnegie Council and Open to Debate's event listings did not load. Columbia CGEP's November calendar is otherwise student roundtables plus a 'Storage Is the New Grid' evening on November 10 with no venue listed, which I left out.

Family: the strongest one is Rella's Laternenlauf on November 8, but note it is in Central Park, not Brooklyn, and it runs at dusk rather than ending by mid-afternoon, which is the nature of a lantern walk. CityKinder runs the Brooklyn version in Prospect Park near the bandshell every November, which would be the better one for Fort Greene, but their page has no 2026 date posted yet. Worth checking citykinder.com in the next week or two. I also could not load the Rock and Roll Playhouse, Jalopy or Brooklyn Children's Museum calendars, which is why the Greenmarket and Governors Island are acting as filler; both are honest but neither is exciting.

One thing I checked and discarded: the German Consulate's 'Open Houses at German International School New York' page lists Sep 30, Oct 26 and Nov 7 with a St. Martin's lantern-crafting event, but those weekdays match 2024, not 2026, and White Plains is outside the five boroughs anyway.

Evidence base was the 279 supplied Instagram captions; everything here traces to a specific post, and I confirmed what I could against ticketing pages. Fully verified (organizer/RA page read): Nowadays Halloween Nonstop (Oct 30–Nov 1), Brutalismus 3000 / B3K Invites NY at Knockdown (Nov 6), and the ZickZack exhibition dates via the Goethe-Institut site. Strong secondary confirmation (DICE/RA/TodayTix listings seen in search results, not fully loaded): Circoloco Nov 1, Elsewhere Halloween, Dope Jams Halloween Ball, Petite Rouge closing Oct 31. DICE event pages block direct fetching, and my web-fetch budget ran out partway through, so several venue-posted items (Knockdown's Haunted Hop, Dax J, Bonobo; Public Records' Oct 30 techno bill; Phoenix bingo; All Night Skate Halloween; Threes Greenpoint; Barbès family show; Butcher's Mouth; NY Emos) rest on the venue's own Instagram post and are marked likely or unverified — prices and exact door times for those are unconfirmed. Gaps I could not close: no dated, confirmed upcoming Daikoku NYC / 1st Motorsport car meet (the Planet X 'FIRST GEAR' event already happened Oct 25 — worth DMing @daikokunyc for the next Chinatown meet), no Muay Thai, kickboxing or boxing card in the five boroughs surfaced in this window, no Union Garage shop-ride date announced for November, no confirmed Nutcracker Rouge or Maccabee Bar (Hanukkah pop-up) on-sale dates, and I could not verify the Red Hook Barnacle Parade start time beyond the Oct 29 date.
